source_test_tool_environment_findings.verified_structural_correlation: 100% of the 9 UNSTABLE_TIMEOUT_TRIAGE mutants are confined to exactly 3 functions in authority_resolver.py: _extract_merge_policy (2/9), _extract_registry_stream_ids (4/9), resolve_input_contract_authority_from_repository (3/9). Zero instability occurred among the 24 raw-timeout candidates in contracts.py (_construct_verified_authority, _seal_verified_authority, _is_well_formed_content_id -- all resolved NOT_REPRODUCED/killed) or the 1 in ownership.py (x_p_run_sort, resolved CONFIRMED_TIMEOUT). Source-verified: resolve_input_contract_authority_from_repository (authority_resolver.py) performs real filesystem I/O directly (Path.is_file(), Path.read_bytes() against the actual Input Contract and Stream Registry artifacts); _extract_merge_policy and _extract_registry_stream_ids are pure in-memory line scanners but are reached exclusively through that same I/O call path in every one of their covering tests. _validate_supported_merge_policy (2 raw-timeout candidates, 0 unstable) operates purely on an already-parsed InputMergePolicy object -- no I/O of its own -- consistent with this pattern.
source_test_tool_environment_findings.verified_covering_test_scope: Fresh tests-for-mutant query (mutmut 3.7.0, coverage collected via one ordinary full-suite clean-test pass at the exact evidence-005.json executable boundary -- no mutation test executed against any of the 9 disputed mutant IDs) shows each of the 9 mutants is covered by 27-42 tests spanning up to 4 files: test_authority_resolver.py, test_historical_authority_resolver.py, test_replay_preparation.py, and (for the 3 resolve_input_contract_authority_from_repository mutants specifically) test_replay_isolation.py::test_external_access_cut_guards_the_real_reachable_boundary -- a test that monkeypatches Path.read_bytes/read_text/open/socket to prove a real filesystem/network access cut is active against the actual production call path. This entire covering-test cluster is distinctively I/O- and access-boundary-centric relative to the rest of the Feature Engine suite, which is predominantly in-memory dataclass/event-object testing.
source_test_tool_environment_findings.verified_timing_uncontended: Fresh, isolated (single-process, no parallel workers) pytest run of the exact 43-test covering set for _extract_merge_policy__mutmut_37 at the evidence-005.json executable boundary: 43 passed in 0.26s, every individual test under 5ms. The full ordinary 414-test suite (same boundary) completes in 14.84s; the slowest 15 individual test durations in the ENTIRE suite are all from test_i13_properties.py (Hypothesis-based property tests, up to 1.03s each) -- none from test_authority_resolver.py or its sibling I/O-touching files, which do not appear in the top-15 slowest at all. test_authority_resolver.py's own 29 tests alone complete in 0.74s uncontended.
source_test_tool_environment_findings.verified_environment_reconfirmation: Fresh isolated worktree at repository boundary 662ed13e68838c17b290754047adb3c0cbf98f62 (evidence-005.json's own executable_boundary); src/tests/tooling trees independently re-verified byte-identical to evidence-005.json's pinned values. Fresh disposable venv: Python 3.13.6, mutmut 3.7.0, pytest 9.1.1 -- all match evidence-005.json's fresh_environment_provenance exactly. mutmut's timeout formula (evidence-005.json anomaly_flag, restated here for reference only): timeout_constant=1.0s, timeout_multiplier=15.0 (a RELATIVE threshold computed from each mutant's own covering-test baseline duration, not an absolute fixed value).
source_test_tool_environment_findings.evidence_gap_disclosed: No raw per-run wall-clock timing/log data for the 9 mutants' own original two protocol runs (evidence-005.json's timeout_triage.records stores only final pass/fail/timeout classification, not duration) is preserved anywhere in this repository -- those runs were ephemeral operations at evidence-005.json's own authoring time and cannot be recovered retroactively. This investigation's own fresh timing measurements (above) are necessarily FROM A DIFFERENT, UNCONTENDED execution context (single worker, this transaction, later in time) and are disclosed as such -- they establish what the covering-test baseline duration looks like absent contention, not what it measured during evidence-005.json's own ~7-parallel-worker full run.
source_test_tool_environment_findings.governance_interpretation_question_not_r: Constitution Chapter 13 §13.10 (Locked, binding) defines a flaky-test policy: forbids retry-until-green, requires quarantine + explicit follow-up for tests 'phụ thuộc timing/ordering/clock', and states an unstable result must not count as passing evidence. This describes ORDINARY test-suite flakiness (a test producing different pass/fail results on unchanged code). Whether §13.10's quarantine mechanism is the intended/applicable EXISTING mechanism for a DIFFERENT phenomenon -- mutmut's own per-mutant TIMEOUT CLASSIFICATION disagreeing across two isolated reruns of MUTATED code under a relative, load-sensitive threshold -- is a genuine interpretive question this investigation does not resolve. Testing Convention v0.17 item 8's own timeout rule ('an unresolved/unreproduced timeout is FAIL -- evidence for that mutant, not a silent pass') is consistent with evidence-005-correction-001.json's STOPPED/UNRESOLVED reading and does not itself supply a resolution path either. This question is flagged for ChatGPT's architecture/governance review, not answered by this executor.

hypotheses_labeled: HYPOTHESIS (plausible, mechanistically reasonable, NOT directly measured under contention -- reproducing 7-way parallel contention would itself require a mutation run and is out of scope): filesystem I/O operations (tmp_path synthetic-repo construction, Path.is_file()/read_bytes() against real artifacts) are disproportionately sensitive to timing variance under heavy concurrent-process resource contention, compared to pure in-memory/CPU-bound work -- explaining why instability concentrated exclusively in the 3 I/O-touching functions despite their comfortably short (0.26s for the full covering set) uncontended baseline duration, while the objectively SLOWEST tests in the whole suite (test_i13_properties.py, CPU-bound Hypothesis tests, up to 1.03s each) showed zero timeout instability at all under the same full run.

HYPOTHESIS (not mechanistically proven, analogous in kind to evidence-005-correction-001.json's own identity.x_deterministic_id__mutmut_3 working hypothesis): mutmut's coverage-based per-mutant test-selection and/or per-mutant baseline-duration measurement may itself carry some run-to-run variance for tests using pytest's tmp_path fixture specifically, independent of pure OS-level resource contention -- not established or refuted by this bounded investigation.

consolidated_wp_result.summary: All 9 of 9 UNSTABLE_TIMEOUT_TRIAGE mutants are classified REQUIRES_GOVERNED_PROTOCOL_DECISION -- not because evidence is insufficient (it is complete and internally consistent for all 9), but because the existing locked timeout-triage protocol, as literally written, defines disagreement as a terminal state with no further resolution step, and no other existing repository authority (Testing Convention item 8, Chapter 13 §13.10) unambiguously supplies an alternative resolution mechanism for this specific phenomenon (mutation-testing timeout-classification instability, as distinct from ordinary test-suite flakiness). This investigation ADDS verified, additive evidence (the I/O-touching structural correlation, the covering-test scope, the uncontended timing baseline) to inform that future governed decision -- it does not itself constitute or authorize one.
consolidated_wp_result.existing_protocol_sufficiency: NOT sufficient on its own to resolve any of the 9 cases -- confirmed by direct re-reading of its own text, corroborated by evidence-005-correction-001.json's MAJ-01 remediation.
